meta.title: Corpus segments and gold census
meta.description: What the scenario corpus is actually made of, what gold is missing, what only looks missing, and how long it has been that way.

props.title: Segments and gold census
props.subtitle: The readback gold was never missing. It was written under a key the projector stopped reading.

props.content: Of 1,159 controller turns that owe a pilot readback, 992 already have one authored in the source. The projector reads a different field, so it reports them as source-silent and the scorer skips them. Only 139 turns are genuinely unwritten, and 130 of those are in a holdout set that was never in the flying denominator.

props.title: Your hypothesis was half right, and the better half
props.content: You asked whether we only owe spoken gold on self-addressed ownship turns. That is exactly the rule, and the system already applies it: 303 party-line and broadcast turns correctly owe nothing. But that is not why the corpus went dark. It went dark because the fix that stopped the projector from inventing gold only taught it to read a new field, and almost nothing writes that field yet.

props.title: Seven segments, not two lanes
props.subtitle: The scorer splits the world into 'starts with pe_' and 'everything else'. That is why a training manual, a hand-built flight library, a transform-validation slice, a holdout set, and a deliberately incoherent speech atlas all score as one lane.

props.caption: Gold census by segment. 'Owed' counts controller-to-ownship turns only.
rows: planeenglish_bulk — one turn each, lifted from the PE manual
partner_raw — never enriched, turns are bare strings

props.content: 'Gold stranded' means the readback is authored under the legacy expected_readback key. 873 of those are already in spoken form and can be copied mechanically; 119 still carry numerals like 'Maintain 3000' and need the digits spelled out before they are speakable.

props.label: Root cause
props.title: What actually happened
props.subtitle: Three changes, none of them wrong on their own.

props.title: The chain
props.summary: Reconstructed from git history and the projector source

items.claim: Until 11 August, the projector built its own answer key by calling the production speech renderer.
items.source: project_eval.py imported render_radio_speech_text and render_compound_readback from modules/
items.detail: The evaluation gold for a readback was generated by the same code being evaluated. Every row passed because both sides came from one source.

items.claim: On 11 August a fix removed those imports so gold could only come from the source files.
items.source: commit 320d5ed19, 'Make evaluation gold independent from runtime semantics'
items.detail: Correct change. It reads only expected_radio_speech_text and marks anything else source-silent.

items.claim: But the corpus writes its readbacks under expected_readback, and always has.
items.source: 421 of 430 partner ownship turns, 96 of 96 PlaneEnglish ownship turns
items.detail: Only 28 turns corpus-wide carry the new key. The fix landed without a migration, so the corpus went from fully scored to barely scored.

items.claim: Nobody noticed for three days because projections are generated artifacts that nobody regenerated.
items.source: committed projections dated 24 June; regenerated today
items.detail: The stale projections on disk still held the fabricated gold, so the baseline kept reporting green until today's promotion chain re-ran the projector.

items.claim: The two fields are not always interchangeable.
items.detail: Where they differ, the legacy field carries numerals ('Maintain 3000', 'N17XX') and the new one carries spoken words. That difference is the whole reason the new field exists.

items.title: Gold rendered by the runtime
items.description: Readback gold for every scored turn was produced by the production renderer being tested. Duration: as long as readback scoring has existed.

items.title: The source-authored field is introduced
items.description: expected_radio_speech_text appears in the projector, but nothing migrates the corpus onto it.

items.title: The source-silent stamp appears
items.description: Turns without source speech begin to be marked, arriving with the BATC holdout work.

items.title: Fail-closed lands
items.description: The projector stops inventing gold. From this moment the corpus is effectively unscored, but the on-disk projections are stale so nothing reports it.

items.title: Detected
items.description: The promotion chain re-projects the whole PlaneEnglish corpus and the scored count collapses from 90 to 7. Three days of silent breakage; eight weeks of a field nobody filled.

props.label: Ledger
props.title: Done and not done
props.subtitle: Against the standing goal: every scenario, every turn.

props.title: Done
props.content: 42 scenarios promoted with full projection, voicing, transcription and rescore. 18-scenario readback wave authored and gated; 16 promoted, 2 waiting. Two scenarios retired as manual prose. Callsign ruling applied to 5 accepted reviews. Direction slot declared in the FMM contract. A deterministic census now exists and gates on exit code.

props.title: Not done
props.content: 992 stranded readbacks not migrated. 139 turns genuinely unwritten. 215 partner scenarios never structured (9,066 turns). 299 scenarios still speak the placeholder callsign. 42 PlaneEnglish scenarios never recertified. 87 genuine engine failures still hidden behind the gold problem.

props.label: Naming
props.title: Files whose names hide what they are
props.subtitle: Recommendations, not renames — nothing has been moved.

props.caption: Suggested renames
rows: 100 files named only by index. Nothing says what phraseology they test.
'v3' is a build version, not content. Reads as a pipeline artifact.
Double underscores and a pipeline stage name. Says nothing about the flights.
Reads like pilot practice data; it is actually a transform-validation slice.
Reads like a flight and scores like one. It is explicitly not a coherent flight.
Engine regression probes sitting in the same folder as real flights, scored in the same denominator.
Zero turns. Not scenarios at all.
move out of sources/partner/ into a fixtures or notes directory

props.content: The probe group matters most. Seven behaviour probes with two to thirteen turns each are averaged into the same score as forty-eight-turn flights, so a probe regression and a flight regression are indistinguishable in the headline number.

props.label: Documentation
props.title: Where the segments should live
props.subtitle: Three places, each with a different job.

props.title: 1. The taxonomy itself, as a spec
props.content: A new docs/specs/corpus-segments-v1.md holding the seven segment definitions, what each is for, which are allowed in the headline score, and the rule that target is a lane tag rather than an addressee. It sits beside the existing baseline-scoring-lanes contract, which already documents corpora but stops at the pe_ prefix split.
props.next: The census tool's docstring is currently the only written definition. Promote it there.

props.title: 2. A pointer in AGENTS.md, not the content
props.content: AGENTS.md is already long and mostly rules. It should gain three or four lines: the segment names, the fact that raw partner scenarios are unstructured rather than merely unenriched, and a link to the spec. Rules in AGENTS.md, definitions in the spec.
props.next: Same treatment the DeBERTa and baseline rules already get.

props.title: 3. The segments as code, so they cannot drift
props.content: The scorer's own filters currently derive the corpus from a string prefix. Segment assignment should move into that module so the report, the gate, and the score all read one definition. The census already implements the classifier; the scorer should import it rather than keep its own.
props.next: Otherwise the doc and the score disagree the first time someone adds a scenario.

props.title: The check you asked for
props.content: uv run python -m tooling.corpus_audit.gold_census — prints the table above, exits 1 when any turn has no gold in either field, and with --strict also fails on stranded gold. It has unit tests. Nothing like it existed: the sibling auditor grades enrichment quality and flags bare digits in slots, but nothing ever asked the plain question 'is the gold there?'
